observations: Each major hotel floor uses a distinct theme and associated traversal, puzzle, trap, and enemy motifs.
Nintendo directs players to investigate suspicious areas and documents visual cues for traps.
The Dark Light reveals invisible furniture, money, power-ups, and hidden-room doors under a consistent tool rule.
Rare ghosts contribute to a persistent gallery collection.
inferences: Strong room themes can support both orientation and expectations about interactions.
A discovery tool remains meaningful when observation identifies where and why to use it.
limits: Official guidance can make clue rules more explicit than blind first-play experience.
ScareScraper and story mode use different procedural and progression constraints.
